evals.prompt: Create a JSON Canvas file showing my project's three-stage pipeline: ingest, transform, publish. Connect them in order.
expected_output_criteria: Produces a valid .canvas JSON document with `nodes` and `edges` arrays
Each node has required JSON Canvas fields: id, type, x, y, width, height
Edges connect ingest → transform → publish with `fromNode` and `toNode` referencing the right ids
Node coordinates are laid out left-to-right (or top-to-bottom) so the flow is readable, not stacked
File parses as JSON without trailing commas or comments

evals.prompt: Open my existing canvas at notes/architecture.canvas and add a new 'monitoring' group around the three observability nodes (logs, metrics, traces). Don't break existing edges.
evals.description: Edit existing canvas; must preserve structure.
expected_output_criteria: Reads the existing canvas before editing rather than overwriting blindly
Adds a `group` node type that visually contains the three observability nodes (correct x/y/width/height bounds)
Does NOT modify or remove any existing edge entries
Preserves existing node ids so unrelated edges remain valid
Returns the resulting canvas as valid JSON the user can save back to disk

evals.prompt: Generate a JSON Canvas for a system architecture: 4 services, each calling a shared database and message bus, with two external APIs feeding service A. Include short notes on each connection.
evals.description: Hard case: multiple connection types, mixed node types, dense layout.
expected_output_criteria: Models services, database, and bus as separate nodes (not collapsed)
Uses appropriate node types (text vs file vs link) per JSON Canvas spec rather than defaulting all to one type
Edges include `label` strings for the connection notes when supported
Layout avoids edge crossings where possible and keeps the database/bus central (not stranded at a corner)
Does not invent JSON Canvas fields outside the spec (e.g., no custom 'connectionType' key)
